sections.title: Policy and access
sections.text:
In Val Gardena, access policy is about the mountain passes and the lifts rather than the villages. A proposal by the Val Gardena and Val Badia municipalities would create a limited-traffic zone on the Passo Gardena (Grödner Joch) from May to October starting in summer 2027, with 150 online-only paid parking spaces for day visitors; it needs final approval from the provincial government [0]. The restriction planned for 1 September 2026 was cancelled in August and the pass stayed open without registration [4]. Instead, the Province's mobility department announced a digital test phase from September 2026 that simulated access permits and limits [1], which Wolkenstein ran from 22 September to 5 October 2026 with voluntary registration of crossings and a questionnaire [2]. The project website says the test has ended and that it did not introduce a permanent traffic rule; the planned zone covers the road from the Miramonti junction to the Mesoles restaurant, and the page does not mention parking [3]. Reports differ on pass traffic: about 6,000 cars on heavily used days according to the ORF, and up to 11,000 vehicles a day according to other 2026 reports [4].

The same crowding is being managed at the lifts. For summer 2026 the Seiser Alm road is closed to private uphill traffic from 09:00 to 17:00, and from 29 June 2026 a parking booking up to six days ahead is required for lots P1 Spitzbühl (15 euros a day for cars) and P2 Compatsch (30 euros) [5]. The Seceda cable car above St. Ulrich requires advance online booking of time slots from summer 2026, after the queues of summer 2025 [6].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The main reported project is a car park for the Seceda lift. In October 2025 Südtirol News reported that plans for the cable car include a car park with 500 car and 25 bus spaces about one kilometre from the valley station, on land owned by the Seceda company, with electric buses taking visitors to the lift. A working group of the company, the Province, the municipality, IDM and the tourism association works on it; the Province still had to approve the doubling of lift capacity, and we found no later confirmation of approval or construction [7]. We found no dated source on new garages in Ortisei, Santa Cristina or Selva, or on charging in the car parks.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The tourism portal lists tariffs for the main car parks. Seceda costs 2.50 euros per 30 minutes from 05:00 to 19:00, with a daily maximum of 30 euros [8]. Setil, next to the Seiser Alm lift, costs 2 euros an hour for cars and 3 euros for campers [10], and Monte Pana P1 in Santa Cristina costs 2 euros an hour and 10 euros a day, paid from 07:00 to 14:00 [11]. The Central garage in Ortisei has about 222 covered spaces and charges 2.50 euros an hour and 20 euros a day; its page does not say who operates it [9]. In July 2026 the three municipalities announced a reduced rate of 0.50 euro an hour for the first five hours for Club Card holders, who are residents, at named public car parks [12]. The tourism portal shows live available-space figures for its ten main car parks, without saying which system feeds them [13].

Our data cover ten car parks with 1,865 spaces from the South Tyrol open-data platform, measured since late September 2026. Occupancy averaged about 38% on weekdays and 39% at weekends, weighted by spaces, but the average hides two kinds of car park. The lift car parks at the valley stations are full or nearly: the Seceda car park and garage (210 spaces) averaged 75%, reached 100% on a Tuesday morning and was full for about 23% of the hours, and Setil (88) was full for about 10%. By contrast Plan de Gralba (400) averaged 8% and Monte Pana P1 (340) 6%, both well below even their best hour. The Dantercëpies garage (500) shows 82% around the clock, with almost no daily variation; we have not been able to confirm that its sensor measures free spaces, so we treat that figure with caution. The measuring period is after the summer season, so these are shoulder-season figures.
